chapter: Barry Martin and New Orleans tours to England
title: What donkey derbies are
summary: The interviewer asks about donkey derbies; Stagg explains the rural English tradition and the Paragon Stakes named after Mike Casimir's brass band.

story.theme_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band monikers
story.community_name: How I got my name: nicknames and band names

blocks.x: Would you explain that donkey derbies?

The donkey derbies? Well, the donkey derbies sort of originated in rural England, way back now, probably in the late 1880s, where they have a group of donkeys, and usually children are jockeys, and they name all these donkeys, and they name their races. They're like a small horse race, and they run only about 20 yards, and only a few shillings on each one. In fact, there's one held every year in a place called Wallington in England, and one of the races is named the Paragon Stakes, after Mike Casimir's Paragon Brass Band. It's like Morris dancing in England. It's part of sort of English heritage, rural English heritage. And really, that's the brass band's saying. Anything else?
